first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior onboarding/signup simplification showed durable early-adoption gains. I would verify the onboarding evidence and the sustainability and quality of promotional-pricing results before ruling out pricing, but prioritize a guarded onboarding test because it addresses both current funnel problems with lower downstream-value risk than discounting.

mid.rationale: Run a standard onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified record shows completion increased 13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation deterioration while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not pursue promotional pricing this cycle: its 18% qualified-revenue lift was offset by a 12% retention decline and failure at the first renewal. Track activation, qualified conversion, time-to-value, and renewal-quality guardrails during the test.

final2.rationale: Run only a tightly targeted defensive pricing test for clearly price-sensitive, at-risk SMB accounts, with strict qualification and renewal-retention guardrails. The competitor threat and doubled churn conversations justify an immediate response, but the verified discount result showed an unsustainable 12% retention decline, so this must not become a broad discount or acquisition strategy. Continue measuring qualified revenue, churn, renewal survival, and contribution margin; stop quickly if retention worsens.
